record_identity.title: DeepSeek exposed an unauthenticated database containing chat histories and secrets

incident_identity.date_basis: Wiz Research publicly disclosed the exposed DeepSeek database on 29 January 2025 and reported that DeepSeek secured it promptly after notification.

summary: Wiz Research found a publicly accessible, unauthenticated ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek. The exposed service provided full database-operation access and contained more than one million lines of logs including chat histories, API secrets, backend details and operational metadata. DeepSeek secured the database after Wiz notified the company; public evidence does not establish whether third parties accessed the data before discovery.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Wiz reports discovering two internet-reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse endpoints with no authentication and full database control. The exposed data included more than one million log lines with chat history, secret keys and backend details. Reuters independently reported the discovery and DeepSeek's rapid remediation after notification.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a material AI-platform data-security failure in surrounding infrastructure rather than a model-behaviour failure. It demonstrates that governance of frontier AI services includes conventional but consequential access control, data custody and operational-security boundaries.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows that an AI service can expose highly sensitive user and operational data through ordinary infrastructure failures even when the model itself is not the failing component. Access control, data custody and deployment security are therefore part of the service's governance boundary.
assessment_boundaries: The evidence does not establish that an unauthorised third party accessed or misused the exposed database before Wiz discovered it.
The complete number of affected users is not public.
The occurrence concerns an infrastructure access-control misconfiguration; the evidence does not establish a failure in model behaviour.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. The preserved evidence establishes a severe backend access-control misconfiguration: internet-reachable ClickHouse endpoints lacked authentication and exposed chat histories, secrets and full database operations. VIGIL-FC-000002 Capability-Authority Conflation was tested but is not established because no AI system or governance process is shown to have treated technical reachability as permission; the database was simply exposed. VIGIL-FC-000031 Authentication-State Continuity Failure is not applicable because no authentication-state transition failed to propagate. VIGIL-FC-000045 Authorised Investigative Evidence-Access Pathway Failure is not applicable because the occurrence is unauthorised public exposure, not absence of a governed route for an already-authorised investigator. The event remains a material infrastructure-security Incident without a precise current selectable Failure Class.

classification_review_provenance.method: deterministic current-taxonomy re-adjudication using preserved Incident evidence and complete VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 class-set review
classification_review_provenance.reviewer: OpenAI ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol under human-directed VIGIL governance
classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000002, VIGIL-FC-000031, VIGIL-FC-000045. Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000002: technical reachability existed, but no system-side inference of permission from reachability is established; VIGIL-FC-000031: no authentication-state transition or stale session state is involved; VIGIL-FC-000045: the occurrence is public unauthenticated exposure, not failure of an authorised investigative evidence-access pathway. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.6; the occurrence remains a conventional but material AI-platform infrastructure access-control failure outside the current mechanism set.
